answer: Each agent stakes an on-chain relic bound to a unique ivory-signed hardware key, and that stake serves as the anchor for its identity score. Creating a sybil requires buying fresh hardware, minting a new relic, and locking the full stake per identity, so a thousand fake agents cost a thousand real stakes. Since reputation and rewards accrue only to staked relics, attackers burn capital with no guaranteed return, making mass identity fabrication economically irrational.
